Docket 1.3.131

**Docket is free to try: run a full audit of any site without a key and see your score, how many problems each area has, and the most important problem in full with its fix. [Buy it once](https://kerr-affiliate-hub.kerrco.workers.dev/buy/docket?src=release-notes), $349, or 4 payments of $87.25, to see all the others, the ranked fix plan and the markup to paste. 30-day refund, no conditions.**

- *A Squarespace owner is no longer told to edit a file they cannot edit.* When a site's robots.txt
  names AI crawlers by names their makers no longer use, the report gave the replacement names and a
  block to paste. On Squarespace, the platform writes robots.txt and owners cannot change it; those
  lines come from Squarespace's own setting for blocking AI crawlers. On a Squarespace site the
  finding now says so, names the setting, and links Squarespace's help page instead of offering
  markup. Everywhere else it is unchanged.
- *Sites built with Webflow are named Webflow.* A Webflow site whose structured data had been pasted
  from a WordPress template was reported as running on WordPress, and another Webflow site showed no
  platform at all. Docket now reads Webflow's own markup, and text inside structured data no longer
  decides the platform.
- *Reviews shown with the writer's name first are found.* A homepage showing two dozen Google reviews,
  each card starting with the reviewer's first name and initial, was told it had no customer reviews.
  Two or more such names near a reviews label now count as reviews.
- *A broken structured-data block is described by what is actually wrong.* When a block closed more
  brackets than it opened, usually because a wrapper was taken out and its closing brackets were left
  behind, the report said it held two separate documents and suggested splitting them. It now says
  which brackets are left over and the line they start on.

99 checks across 13 areas.
